title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a working page from the Teichmüller-groupoid notes, numbered (5) by Grothendieck. It sits between two unrelated administrative sheets (pp. 31 and 33). It contains three fragments.

(i) The boxed relation (2''). It reads c̃^ω(λ p̃_a^ω) = c̃_a^ω(λ p̃_{ω'}). It is a compatibility condition between 'transport' or cocycle data c̃, indexed by a combinatorial rotation ω and an element a. The data are evaluated on 'paths' or 'points' p̃ twisted by λ. The marginal French says, roughly: 'in the presence of (1), this is a consequence of (2'), which amounts to the validity of (2') when one takes this into account.' So Grothendieck is reducing a list of axioms: (2'') is redundant given (1) and (2'). This is routine bookkeeping in setting up a presentation by generators and relations.

(ii) A small diagram. Two arrows μ, μ' go Q → Q^∨ (a 'φ' is also written), and two arrows μ̌, μ̌' go Q^∨ → Q. The composites are λ = μ̌μ and λ' = μ̌'μ'. He records that λ = λ' is equivalent to μ̌'^{-1}μ̌ = μ'μ^{-1}. This is the comparison of two factorizations of the same automorphism λ of Q through the 'dual' Q^∨. Normalizing μ' = 1 gives μ̌ = μ̌'μ', hence μ̌' = μ̌. In context this is likely a change of rigidification or base point: Q may be a vertex or base-point object, Q^∨ its dual or opposite, and λ a monodromy or orientation-reversal element. This reading is a guess.

(iii) Below a rule, a figure and a boxed identity. The figure is a cycle of vertices, each carrying a small loop (a ribbon-graph or 'carte' picture). It shows half-edge or arc labels ã_r, ã_{r1}, ã_{r'}, ã_{r1'}, b̃_r, points R̃_r, R̃_{r1}, Q̃_a, and a shaded triangular 2-cell bounded by ã_r, b̃_r and a chord to ã_{r1'}.

The boxed identity is Ã_{ω''r''} Ã_{ω'''r''} ⋯ Ã_{r''} = Ã_{ω r1} Ã_{ω^{-1} r1} ⋯ Ã_{r1}. It equates the products of generators along an ω-orbit (going around a face or vertex) read from two different starting half-edges. The overbraces label the pieces as μ_{ẽ_a} and μ_{ẽ'_r}. This is the standard 'face relation' in a presentation of a fundamental groupoid of a combinatorial surface, together with its independence of the starting point (cyclic conjugation).

A crossed-out attempt B̃_{ω''r} B̃_{ω'r} ⋯ B̃_r = μ_r, and an empty triangle sketch, show he was trying an alternative normalization: the product around a cell equals a given element μ_r. Overall the page is part of verifying the coherence of a generators-and-relations description of Teichmüller-type groupoids built from maps (cartes).
errors: The marginal expression '(μ'^{-1}μ)^{-1}' does not type-check against μ'μ^{-1}. If μ, μ': Q→Q^∨, then μ'μ^{-1} is an endomorphism of Q^∨, while (μ'^{-1}μ)^{-1} = μ^{-1}μ' is an endomorphism of Q. It is either a different quantity jotted down or a slip; it only coincides in a commutative or identified setting.
The second boxed product mixes exponent notation (ω, ω^{-1}) with prime notation (ω'', ω'''). The indexing of the orbit is inconsistent as written, which is typical of scratch work.
The crossed-out B̃-relation was abandoned, so the intended normalization is incomplete on this page.

ideas.what: Reduction of axiom (2'') to (1) and (2') for cocycle/transport data c̃ indexed by a rotation ω
ideas.modern_name: redundancy of relations in a groupoid presentation / cocycle conditions

ideas.what: Comparing two factorizations λ = μ̌μ of an automorphism through a dual object Q^∨, and normalizing μ' = 1
Product of generators along an ω-orbit of half-edges (a face of a map) is independent of starting point; used as the face relation
ideas.modern_name: face/cell relations in the presentation of the fundamental groupoid of a ribbon graph (combinatorial map)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical combinatorial group theory; for Teichmüller/ribbon graphs: Penner, Harer, Kontsevich (1980s–90s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), cartes and the Teichmüller tower, in general form only

deep.surprise_reason: Routine scratch verification of relations and normalizations for a combinatorial presentation of a Teichmüller-type groupoid via maps. Nothing beyond standard face relations and gauge normalization is visible.

The overbraces read μ_{ẽ̃_a} (over the left side) and μ_{ẽ̃'_r} or similar (over the right side).
The marginal French is plausibly: 'en présence de (1), c'est une conséquence de (2'), qui équivaut à la validité de (2') en le prenant en compte'.
